_note: crafter__crafter.json played through eight buttons instead of seventeen keys, which is the control scheme crafter-for-brain-scan v0.33 uses in the scanner (core.py:ButtonMapper, frontend_pygame.py:KEYMAP). Same env, same level: gym/crafter's CrafterMenu-v0 is Crafter-v0 under a wrapper where six actions keep a button of their own and the other ten sit in a cursor the subject cycles to. Install as for crafter__crafter.json, fork included; read that config's notes first, since only what differs is written down here.
_menu_note: The wrapper's action space is Discrete(19): crafter's own 17, then cycle (17) and confirm (18). W advances the cursor and steps the env with noop, A performs the action the cursor is on; both draw the cursor over the player for that one frame. The cost of a look is a turn, as it is in the rig: a free cycle would make all ten actions reachable for one press. The npz records the button in 'actions' and the engine's action in 'env_action', plus 'menu_idx' and 'menu_sel' read after the press, and action_names covers all 19 so the button column decodes. Two deviations from the rig, both deliberate: the cursor shows while the last press was cycle or confirm rather than for 3 wall-clock seconds (--menu-s), because a turn-based block repaints only on a press and has no clock to fade against, and this version is reconstructible from the logged actions alone; and the cursor sits at 3.5/9 of the frame height, the centre of the played area above crafter's own two HUD rows, which is where the rig puts it too.
_keys_note: Eight keys, the ones the rig's own frontend uses (frontend_pygame.py:KEYMAP -- D and S beside the arrows, W and A for the two menu buttons), so a subject who has practised in crafter-for-brain-scan keeps their fingers. cycle and confirm have to be written as the literal ids 17 and 18: they are not crafter actions and nothing else names them. No '' entry, because turn_based means the loop steps only on a press. The ten menu actions are not listed anywhere: they are whatever the action space has left over, so a crafter that gained an action would put it in the menu rather than drop it.
_pacing_note: turn_based is true, which is the whole point of this variant and the one place it parts company with both crafter__crafter.json and the rig. Eight buttons cost more presses per action than seventeen keys, so a fixed cadence would spend the survival clock on menu cycling; here the world advances once per press and never otherwise, so the run is paced by the subject and every step is a decision. fps 15 is then a polling rate, not a game speed: it bounds how long a press waits to be seen (~67 ms), and it is what the other turn-based DBP configs use. latched_keys is irrelevant under turn_based -- the loop already reads keydowns -- and is left off. The rig has no turn-based mode at all: it runs a fixed 5 Hz cadence (frontend_pygame.py --cadence), so wall-clock comparisons with a rig run do not transfer, and only the action sequences do.
_size_note: size stays 384, not the rig's GAME_PX 288. 384 is an integer half of the 768-pixel display height and 288 is not, and display.draw_frame scales unfiltered, so 288 would smear the pixel art and the HUD counters first. Nothing about the game depends on it; crafter renders its 9x9 view at whatever size it is given.
_state_note: state_stride 25 counts frames, and a frame is now a press rather than 400 ms, so anchors fall every 25 presses instead of every 10 s. The block is also much shorter in frames than a 2.5 fps one of the same duration, so both the npz and the anchor count shrink.

text: tools, eat, drink, sleep, and stay alive.
The world waits for you: it moves one step each
time you press a button, and not otherwise.
The menu holds the ten actions with no button of
their own: place stone, table, furnace, plant, and
make a wood / stone / iron pickaxe or sword. W
moves the cursor and shows it over your character;
A performs it. Moving the cursor also costs a turn.
